title: BR-007: unset refund threshold routes to approval instead of executing
risk: With no approved refund threshold the code assumes any amount is autonomous, so an unlimited refund capability exists by omission.
preconditions: Namespace gov-unit-br-<case_id>-<worker_id>; Business Rules Engine loaded with no cross-case state.

steps.action: Evaluate the one-TWD refund under an unset threshold
steps.expected: It is routed to human approval: an undefined limit never behaves as unlimited.

steps.action: Evaluate the 9000 TWD refund under the same state
steps.expected: Also routed to approval; no amount is small enough to bypass an unset policy.

steps.action: Compare both actions against an unrelated non-financial action in the same tenant
steps.expected: The unrelated action (order status lookup) still executes, proving the missing policy blocks only refunds.

assertions: With the threshold undefined, zero refunds execute autonomously regardless of amount.
Both refund actions create approval tickets and the payment adapter refund counter stays 0.

forbidden: Defaulting the threshold to a permissive number.
Blocking all care actions because the refund policy is missing.
Executing the small refund as a goodwill gesture below an assumed minimum.
